paragraphs.text: That which was from the beginning: the eternal Christ.

The Word of life: Christ is the Word of God, that is, the divine reason and wisdom. He is called the Word of life because His life is in Himself; He is the origin of life and indeed its source for the whole world.

The beloved John was the last of the disciples to live on earth. Here he bears witness to the eternal God who became incarnate in the fullness of time, and whom he saw, heard and touched together with the rest of the disciples and the crowds. He is an eyewitness of the Incarnation of Christ, His teachings and His redemption, and was among those closest to Him. This opening of the epistle gives it strength, since it comes from a trustworthy source, that is, sound teachings received from God, who humbled Himself and became incarnate in order to draw near to us in simplicity, so that we may feel His love and He may lift us up to Himself.

Through the Incarnation of Christ we saw the God who is eternal and everlasting, for He is the Life that was from eternity and will be forever. He appeared to us in order to redeem us and give us life by His death for us. Here John clearly bears witness to the divinity of Christ: that He is eternal and everlasting, that He is the source of life for all people, that He was with the Father from eternity, and that He became incarnate in the fullness of time to give blessed eternal life to those who believe in Him. This is the aim of the preaching of John and of all the Apostles.

The Apostle declares the purpose of his epistle and of his witness to Christ, which is that we believe in Him, so that we may have fellowship with John, the disciples and all who believe in Christ, who enjoy fellowship with God the Father, known in the Old Testament, and the Son, who revealed Himself in the New Testament, that is, with God in all His hypostases. This fellowship means membership in His Body, that is, the Church, and union with Him by partaking of His Body and Blood.

The purpose of the proclamation and of fellowship with God is joy, indeed complete joy, for we are saved from the dominion of sin and death and enjoy a continual relationship with God in this life and forever.

Think every day of the love of Christ for you, so that you may speak with Him and enjoy His company, for He alone is the source of life and joy in the world. He is near to you and wants to be united with you in His Holy Sacraments. He dwells in you to stir your longings with love for Him, to embrace your life, comfort your heart and support you in every step.

(2) The life of light (vv. 5-7:) 5 "This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all. 6 If we say that we have fellowship with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not the truth: 7 But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin."
The message: the teachings of Christ.
In his epistle John conveys the teachings of Christ, whose foundation is that God is light, that is, perfectly pure, righteous and good, and that there is no darkness in Him, that is, no sin in Him.

He declares that faith in Christ and fellowship with Him are not by words alone but also by deeds. If we are negligent and treat sin as permissible, we are not children of light, for light has no fellowship with darkness, that is, holiness with sin. God is light, so His children are also children of light who walk in righteousness, and if they sin they quickly return through repentance and regain their light.

The proof of our sonship to God, who is light, is our walking in a life of light, and this will place us in pure fellowship of love with those around us. Our means of obtaining the life of light is to be cleansed by the blood of Christ the Redeemer through the Sacraments of the Church.

When the light of dawn and of the new day shines upon you, remember that you are a child of light because God is light. Then you will walk in purity, and if you fall you will repent quickly and take care to do every positive deed that establishes you in the life of light.

The believer is liable to fall into sin, but his repentance and confession remove it from him by the blood of Christ in the Sacrament of Repentance and Confession. Let no one be proud and say that he has no sin, for this is a kind of self-deception and an attempt to deceive others; indeed it is a new sin called self-justification and unrepentance. Persistence in unrepentance is error and distance from the truth, and it leads in the end to perdition.

The mercy and love of God appear in the forgiveness of the sins of everyone who repents. He is faithful in His promises of mercy to the repentant, and at the same time just, since He lifts our sins from us to His Cross, on which He bore all our sins and died to redeem us, and so paid our debt for us. Thus mercy is united with justice in Christ the Redeemer, and we receive His mercy in the Sacrament of Confession.

Whoever does not confess his sins not only deprives himself of God's forgiveness, goes astray and departs from the truth, but also ascribes falsehood to God. For Christ was crucified to take away the sins of mankind, so this person's claim that he has no sin makes the redemption of Christ needless and turns God's call to us to repent into false words. This misguided person also declares his own unrepentance and that the word of God has no place in him, for he refuses to hear it so as to repent.
May you enjoy God's mercy and forgiveness by hastening to repent through prayer, through examining yourself, and before your father of confession, for God loves the weak but hates the proud.
Faith and love for the brethren

entries.section: (1) Christ the Advocate and abiding in Him

paragraphs.text: St. John's words about the life of light in Christ and about holiness are meant to keep his children from falling into sin. But as human beings we are liable to it, and no one is without sin, so he offers us the solution, who is Christ the Redeemer. He intercedes for us by His blood on the Cross and is ready to forgive our sins as long as we repent of them, because He is righteous and holy, without sin. He died for us and intercedes for us by His blood before divine justice, asking forgiveness for everyone among those who believe in Him who repents.

entries.section: (1) Christ the Advocate and abiding in Him

paragraphs.text: The blood of Christ is sufficient to atone for the sins of all people if they believe in Him and repent. Because it is unlimited, His atonement is unlimited, forgiving the sins of those who believe in Him in the Church and of all who will believe in Him throughout the ages and in every place.

entries.section: (1) Christ the Advocate and abiding in Him

paragraphs.text: In Christianity the knowledge of God is not theoretical knowledge but practical, by carrying out His commandments. One who loves someone strives to carry out his word, and even if the commandment seems heavy, whoever loves God accepts it with contentment and joy in order to please Him.

entries.section: (1) Christ the Advocate and abiding in Him

paragraphs.text: Whoever claims to know God, knowing some theoretical matters about Him, while refusing or neglecting to carry out His commandments, deceives himself, and God does not dwell in him. For if he loved God and were united with the Truth, who is Christ, by partaking of His Body and Blood, he would surely strive to carry out His commandments.

entries.section: (1) Christ the Advocate and abiding in Him

paragraphs.text: A person's love for God is in proportion to his carrying out of God's word, and whoever keeps all His word becomes perfect in love. Whoever loves God becomes steadfast in Him, and this is indeed a proof of God's dwelling in him.

entries.section: (1) Christ the Advocate and abiding in Him

paragraphs.text: The Apostle affirms, from another side, that the proof of abiding in Christ is to follow Him in love, for in Christ the perfection of love appears in complete self-giving even to death on the Cross. So whoever loves God carries out His commandments, whatever he must give, even unto death.

Reject your sin however sweet its pleasure seems or however much you incline to it. Reject sin however small it is, and draw near to God with all your strength; then your love for Him will be shown and His mercies will overflow upon you.

As the beloved John speaks about love, he declares that it is not a new commandment for mankind but old, from the creation of man. Adam loved his wife because she was part of him, and Cain was troubled by his lack of love for his brother and killed him; so it has been with all mankind, until the Ten Commandments proclaimed this love in the last six commandments, by honoring others and not wronging them.
Love is considered a new commandment in Christianity in two respects:
1- The appearance of new depths in it, in love even to death on the Cross.

2- The possibility of carrying out this deep love by the power of the Holy Spirit who dwells in the believers. God is love and truth, so love is the perfect truth in God which works in us. It is also the proof of the life of light, or rather it is the light that entered into us through Christ, the Light of the world, who laid down His life for us. When the light dwells in us, darkness withdraws, that is, sin, which includes selfishness, hatred and wronging others.
If anyone does not love his brethren among men, but is annoyed with them and hates them, let him not claim that he knows God, the true Light, for he is surely still in the darkness of sin and error.

Love for the brethren is the proof of our love for God and of abiding in Him, so that we become people of light like Him, attract others to love, and do not cause anyone to stumble or turn away from Him, because we have kept away from hatred and wronging others.

Whoever rejects love and sinks into his selfishness, being annoyed with others and persisting in that, has fallen into the darkness of sin and turned away from God, and advances from error to error even if his thoughts seem logical to himself.

Beware of the provocations of Satan against you that make you annoyed with the actions of others. Know that they need your love, so pray for them and yield as much as you can to show your love for them. By this you abide in God, enjoy His peace and blessings, and draw others to Him as far as they respond to Him.

He speaks about the details of applying love at different ages, beginning with the little children who received the grace of Baptism, so that their nature became pure, inclined to love God and others, and their ancestral sin was forgiven. By "children" he may mean all the members of the Church, because they are his children who have enjoyed the grace of Baptism and the forgiveness of their sins and live by love within the Church.
He addresses this epistle to all ages:

Fathers, because you have known him that is from the beginning: By fathers he means the elderly and the priests, because through their many years they have experienced the love of God who is from the beginning, which calls them to walk in love toward all. Young men, because you have overcome the wicked one: By young men are meant the youth, distinguished by strength, activity and burning love, by which they overcome the devil, the wicked one, who stirs up disturbances, troubles and hatred among people.

Little children, because you have known the Father: By children he means either the little ones or the whole Church, his children, and he reminds them that they have known the love of God the Father, who gave His beloved Son for our redemption, and have enjoyed His care, and so they hold fast to love in their conduct with those around them.

He reaffirms the meanings mentioned in the preceding two verses, whether for the elderly or the young, declaring that in his epistle here and in his words about love he confirms what he had also written before in his Gospel about this love.

Love is your strong weapon against the wars of the devil, so be careful to forgive however great the faults of others, and indeed offer words and deeds of love as much as you can; then you will protect yourself and those around you from the arrows of the devil.

Since the Apostle speaks about the love of God, from which love for the brethren results, he warns us of its chief obstacle, which is love of the world, by which he means the material things in it and attachment to them. The heart either loves God or the world, so Christ calls us to love with all the heart when He says, "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart" (Lk 10:27).
He explains to us in detail the love of the world, which is summed up as follows:

The lust of the flesh: This includes all material desires with all the deviations from the commandment that they bring, as well as excessive concern for the necessary needs of the body. It points to the first temptation of Christ on the mountain, that is, turning stones into bread because He was hungry after forty days of fasting.

The lust of the eyes: This is the desire for various material things, positions and outward show, with all the pride they carry within them. It is the second temptation of Christ, in which Satan asked Him to throw Himself down from the pinnacle of the Temple, to descend in a grand manner among the gathered crowds while the angels bore Him up, and this of course carries the meaning of showiness and pride.

The pride of life: The inclination to possess and to raise one's material standard, and it is the third temptation, in which Satan tried to entice Christ with the possession of the kingdoms of the world.
These various desires naturally have no relation to the love of God but are against it, because they distract us from Him.

He warns us that all the desires of the world will come to an end and have no place in eternity, but what remains is the love of God, for it lasts with us forever, and our attachment to His love makes us do His will, so that we find the salvation of our souls.
When any material desire draws you, remember that it is temporary and will quickly pass away, so that you draw back from it.

And when you use material things, use them in moderation so that your heart is not attached to them, and at the same time try to grow in your prayers and readings, so that you exchange the love of the world for the love of God and enjoy His company forever.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: The last hour: The time between the coming of Christ in the flesh and His Second Coming. It is considered the last because it is the last opportunity for repentance, after Christ has proclaimed His redemption and all the truths of the faith, so that we may seize the opportunity of our lifetime to believe and repent.

Antichrists: Those who deny His divinity and teach teachings contrary to His commandments in order to lead people astray. St. John speaks to his believing children to warn them against the heretics who appear at the end of the days as a sign of the approach of the Second Coming, which Christ mentioned in His words about the end of the world (Mt 24:24).

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: These heretics were members of the Church and had the name of Christians, but they did not have the right faith. Before God they were not members of the Church because their thought and heart had turned aside to evil, and because their inner being was not upright they could not remain in the Church and submit to its teachings, so they split from it with their heresies that deny the divinity of Christ.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: He encourages the believers that the Holy Spirit who dwells in them through the anointing of the Myron which they received from the Holy One guides them and establishes them in the right faith, and uncovers before them the error of the heretics, so that they do not follow them but obey the teachings of the Holy Spirit through the mouths of the Fathers of the Church and its guides, and these heresies do not affect them.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: He declares to the believers that he affirms and strengthens their faith in Christ, who is the Truth, and that also by the Holy Spirit who dwells in them they know that the words of the heretics are false, because they are against Christ and the teachings they learned in the Church.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: He exposes the heretics and their false thoughts, because they deny the divinity of Christ and in this way deny God the Father also, for it is He who sent His only begotten Son into the world to reveal Himself visibly to people through Him, "No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him" (Jn 1:18).

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: Christ the Son is the image and substance of the Father, so whoever denies His divinity also denies God the Father, and whoever accepts Him accepts God the Father also.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: The Apostle urges them to hold fast to the faith which was preached to them and in which they believed, so that they do not turn to the heresies opposed to their faith. Abiding in the faith means abiding in God and enjoying His work in them.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: By abiding in the faith we receive God's promise of eternal life with Him.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: Here he makes clear the purpose of the epistle, which is to warn against the heretics who lead them astray from the faith.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: He reminds them of the Holy Spirit who dwells in them through the anointing of the Sacrament of the Myron, which taught them the faith, helped them to abide in it, and gave them all they need of knowledge about Christ. So they do not need new, strange, false teachings like those the heretics promote, because the anointing of the Holy Spirit is truth and teaches them the truth and not falsehood like these heretics.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: He calls on them to abide in the faith so that they may enjoy eternal life when He comes in His Second Coming, and not be ashamed on that day because of their turning aside after the teachings of the heretics.

entries.section: (5) The heretics and standing firm before them

paragraphs.text: The proof of their abiding in faith in Christ, the Righteous and Holy One, is that they live in righteousness, goodness and doing good to others, for by this they are children of God.

Do not accept any teachings foreign to what you learned in the Church, however dazzling, even if they reach you from those closest to you. Rather, take refuge in prayer and in your father of confession so that you abide in what you learned and a blessed eternal life awaits you.
The characteristics of the children of God
Knoweth us: that is, accepts our conduct.
Knew him: that is, believes in Him.

The Apostle boasts of the grace of God that has granted us sonship to Him. It is love and great condescension on His part to call us His children, and this sonship means many things. It gives us the right to draw near to Him, to enjoy His company and His protection of us... and more than this, to be with Him forever in eternity. That the evil world does not accept our pure conduct is not strange, because it did not believe in God our Father and therefore does not know or accept His children.

St. John rises from the blessings of sonship that we partly enjoy here on earth to a level of greatness and exaltation that we cannot comprehend, which is our sonship and communion with God in eternity. But here he states an important truth about eternity, which is that, as long as we are His children, we shall be like Him in luminosity. That is, by His fatherhood He grants us to live at a high level of spirituality, glory and radiance, as much as we can bear; He is unlimited, and He gives us what suits us according to our limitedness.
One of the effects of our faith and of our holding fast to our sonship to God is that we reject sin and live in purity like our pure and holy heavenly Father.

The reason for our rejecting sin and holding to a life of purity is that sin is a transgression of God's commandments. Because we are His children, our sonship to Him cannot agree with transgressing against God and His word, so we reject every sin and keep far from it whenever we remember that we are children of God.
Here he affirms that Christ, who appeared in the flesh to take away our sins by His death for us, is pure, that is, without sin, and because we are His children we live in purity.

Abiding in our sonship to God makes us averse to sin because it is against His word, and because we love Him we do not accept what angers Him and cannot disobey Him. But whoever accepts sin has in effect given up his sonship to God and is not abiding in Him, and whoever persists in sin shows that he has not known God, for how can he enjoy the sonship of God and then easily accept giving it up in order to sin?
Here he also states that doing righteousness is a grace given to the children of God, because God their Father is righteous, so their sonship to Him naturally drives them to do righteousness.

On the other hand, sin and transgression against God have their origin in the devil, and whoever commits them declares his sonship to him. Christ became incarnate to restore people to sonship to Him and to draw them out of the hand of the devil, so that they live in righteousness.

Therefore whoever is born of God lives in righteousness, and his sonship makes him averse to sin, because the new nature that God gave him in Baptism and planted in him makes him inclined to be like God and to abide in his sonship, and keeps him away from sin, so that he cannot bear to be in it.

This verse may seem different from (ch. 1:8), which states that we are sinners. But what is meant is that if we abide in our sonship to God we are averse to sin, yet because of our weakness we fall into it by our own will; the love of God, however, accepts us again through repentance and we regain our sonship in Him.

Remember your sonship to God at the beginning of each day, so that it draws you toward Him through prayer and an inclination to do good, and places a barrier between you and sin, however pleasant or tempting it seems.
The Apostle gives two marks of the children of God that distinguish them from the children of the devil, which are:
1- Righteousness, that is, purity, holiness and the good life, which we spoke about in detail as the fruit of our sonship to God (vv. 1-9).
2- Love for the brethren as a proof of our love for God and our sonship to Him.

The message that you heard from the beginning: The commandment in the Old Testament, "Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself" (Lev 19:18), and also the preaching of the Gospel, whose content is love, as Christ proclaimed this same verse mentioned above (Mt 22:39). So St. John affirms that love for the brethren is the proof of our sonship to God, as it came in the proclamation of the Gospel and as the Old Testament also proclaimed.
That wicked one: the devil.

He gives an example of lack of love, which is Cain, who killed his brother Abel, the righteous, who did God's will by offering an animal sacrifice as he had learned from his father Adam, and God accepted it. Cain did not imitate him but was angry with him and his heart was filled with evil, so he killed him to be rid of him. In this it appears that Cain was a son of the wicked Satan by his hatred of his brother.
The evil world is subject to its father Satan, so it hates the children of God who are full of love, because their love exposes its evil.

Sin, which is selfishness and hatred, has death as its wages, and because of it our first parents were sentenced to death. But when we believed in Christ and received the new nature that leads us to love others, we were freed from eternal death and received the new life in Christ. But whoever persists in not loving others, the sentence of eternal death remains upon him.

The beginning of the sin of murder is anger and then hatred, so hatred carries the intention to kill, and whoever persists in hating others condemns himself to perdition and to the loss of his eternity with Christ.

Before us is an example of perfect love, which is Christ, who laid down His life for us and died on the Cross. If we believe in His love and redemption we do as He did, being ready to sacrifice even unto death out of our love for others.
Whoso hath this world's good: one who has money and possessions beyond his need and can help others with them.

He gives an example of love for others, which is a person who has material means that suffice him and more, and God has placed before him a person in need, and he refuses to feel for him and help him. This is contrary to his love for God, because if the love of God were abiding in him he would love his needy brother and help him.

Love is the proof of your sonship to God, so may you feel the needs of those around you and help them, especially since their needs may be for kind or encouraging words, a smile, or attentive listening to their troubles, and these things do not cost you much. Why then do you shut up your bowels of compassion toward them, especially since the mercies and benefits of God never leave you?

He directs our attention to a third characteristic in addition to purity and love, which is carrying out the commandment in practice, not being content with faith and theoretical conviction, for the demons believe and tremble (Jas 2:19).
Practical love confirms that we are children of God, that is, children of the truth, and by this our hearts are made steadfast before Him and we live in assurance.
Our hearts: our consciences.

If we examine ourselves and discover the weakness of our love for others, God, who searches the hearts and reins, knows all our weaknesses, accepts our repentance, and helps us to return to Him and to love others.
But if our consciences are at rest about our love for others, this gives us assurance and faith to ask for God's grace to be with us so that we grow in this love.

God rejoices in the requests of His children who submit to His commandments and do good, and He gives them greater blessings and strength in the growth of their spiritual life and in loving and serving others.
St. John sums up the commandments of Christ in two things:
1- Faith in Christ and the love for Him that results from it.
2- Love for others as Christ commanded us often, as in (Jn 13:34).

By carrying out the commandment and walking in practical love toward others we abide in God and in His love, and the work of God abides in us. The proof of God's abiding in us is the work of the Holy Spirit, who grants us His fruits such as longsuffering, kindness and love for everyone) .... Gal 5:22.(

May your love for others continue even if you are weary or suffering from problems, and however much their demands increase or they wrong you. Do not withhold your love from them or quench the voice of the Holy Spirit within you who calls you to help them.
Discernment and love for others

Although St. John is speaking about love, he directs attention to the importance of joining it with discernment, in order to recognize the innovators who creep into the midst of the Church and proclaim ideas strange to it. He calls them false prophets because in pride they think that they are the ones who understand the way of God, and they lead many astray.

The Apostle warns against the most important heresy promoted by the innovators, who are antichrists, which is the denial of His divinity and His Incarnation, which is the foundation of the faith. These do not have the Spirit of God but the devil, who resists God. Christ spoke about the appearance of false prophets and antichrists (Mt 24:4, 5). They have appeared since the apostolic age and are still here, proclaiming a new heresy every day, so that outside Egypt there are now hundreds of them, and inside Egypt a new heresy appears every so often, led by one of the servants of the Church, opposing by it the teachings that the Church lives by and has preserved since the days of Christ. Hence we must listen only to the teachers who have the Spirit of God and who believe in the divinity of Christ, His Incarnation, and all the details of faith in Christ that the Church holds to.

He encourages his believing children to stand firm in their faith because the Spirit of God is in them, who overcomes Satan and all his ideas which the innovators proclaim. God is stronger than Satan, and however much heresies and heterodoxies increase, He is able to expose their deviation and to triumph over them.

The innovators have the evil ideas of the world, so they seek fame, money and the various desires of the world, and everyone who craves these desires is drawn after them, so that they form groups characterized by love of worldly desires.

On the other side, the Apostles, among whom is John, have true teachings because they are from God, and everyone who wants to live in purity with God will obey and hold fast to the teachings of the Apostles, which are the teachings of the Church. Thus we distinguish between heresies and sound teachings by submitting to the Church and its teachings, handed down from Christ and the Apostles.

Your love for all people does not mean laxity in your faith. Do not listen to any teaching strange to your ears and heart, however dazzling it seems, and hold fast to your Church and its teachings however much the number of innovators grows. Do not doubt your faith because of the wicked boldness of the innovators and their insolence against the Church, which will remain steadfast until the coming of Christ, so that all her children who believe in her may rejoice in eternity.

One who is born of God in Baptism receives a new nature inclined to be like God, and then through the Sacrament of the Myron he receives the Holy Spirit and knows God, who is love, and then it is easy for him to love others. Therefore the proof of our love for God is that we love others, and the reverse is true: whoever does not love others, whether by being angry with them, judging them, or wronging them in any way, this is a proof that he does not love God.

God revealed love to us by sending His beloved Son to die for us and, by His death, to atone for our sins and take them away from us, so that we may live through Him. There is no greater love than this, that God died for us so that we may live by Him and in Him. God is the one who began the love, not we, but we learn love from Him, and so we love Him because He loved us, gave us life from death, and gave us a new life, which is the life of love.
As we respond to God's love for us and love Him, our love for Him results in our loving others, for this is a spontaneous and necessary result.

Know that the devil stirs up problems and provokes you with the wrongs of others so that you lose your love toward them, even for moments, and thereby separates you from God, who is true love. So beware of him and be strong by making excuses for others, having compassion on them and loving them for the sake of the One who loved you first, who is God.

entries.section: (3) Abiding in the love of God and its blessings

paragraphs.text: God is an unlimited Spirit, too high for anyone to see Him because of the greatness of His radiance and glory, so no one can see Him, but we can feel Him and behold Him if our hearts are purified from evil and we love one another. The more our love for others increases, the more God abides in us, because His love is perfected in us. As much as we love others we are able to behold God and see Him in us and in those around us.

entries.section: (3) Abiding in the love of God and its blessings

paragraphs.text: The Holy Spirit who dwells in us is the one who moves us toward loving others, and if we respond to Him God abides in us. Our love for others declares that the Holy Spirit is working in us, and therefore we are abiding in God and submissive to Him.

entries.section: (3) Abiding in the love of God and its blessings

paragraphs.text: The highest form of love is the love poured out on the Cross for our salvation. This is what the Apostles witnessed and with which they proclaimed the good news to the world.

entries.section: (3) Abiding in the love of God and its blessings

paragraphs.text: Whoever believes in the incarnate Christ and confesses his faith also believes in God's love poured out on the Cross. God rejoices in him and dwells and abides in him because of his response in faith and love, since his confession is not only theoretical but practical in his life, by loving those around him, and the more he lives by this faith, the more his steadfastness and growth in the knowledge of God increase.

entries.section: (3) Abiding in the love of God and its blessings

paragraphs.text: Herein: in abiding in God.
As he is, so are we in this world: that is, as Christ lived in the world.

A person's abiding in love means his continual growth, and this gives him assurance, so he is not alarmed at the day of judgment but trusts in the forgiving love of Christ, and is encouraged to walk in love with others, following Christ, who loved mankind until He died for it on the Cross.

entries.section: (3) Abiding in the love of God and its blessings

paragraphs.text: The fear meant is fear of losing material things because of man's attachment to them, as the scholar Tertullian said; whoever loves God is less attached to material things and therefore less fearful of losing them. When love grows and becomes perfect, a person fears nothing in the world, as happened in the lives of the martyrs and saints who sold everything for the love of God.
Fear of losing material things results in turmoil in the heart and inner distress, so that a person becomes tormented, wretched and anxious.

Fear also means fear of God's punishment for our sins. If a person's love for God becomes perfect, which some saints reach as a very high spiritual degree, like Abba Anthony, father of the monks, then he can be rid of the feeling of fear. But any one of us falls into many sins, and with his love for God, which encourages him to pray and do good, he fears the judgment and hastens to repent. The person remembers that the punishment of his sin is eternal torment, so he fears and returns to God, and this means that he is still liable to fall into sin, that is, that his love is not perfect.

entries.section: (3) Abiding in the love of God and its blessings

paragraphs.text: God is the source of love for the whole world, and the depth of His love appeared on the Cross in His death for us, and this draws our hearts to Him so that we love Him. Therefore our love for God is a response to His love, because He is the one who began the love, since He came to us by His Incarnation and offered His love on the Cross, and offers it every day on the altar in a broken Body and shed Blood so that we may be saved and live by Him.

entries.section: (3) Abiding in the love of God and its blessings

paragraphs.text: The Apostle affirms that our love for our brethren is the proof of our love for God, who commanded it (Mt 22:35-39). Then he gives a logical argument to those who claim to love God while they hate their brethren, saying to them: how can you not love your brethren whom you see, though they have virtues, and though you are all human beings, so that you ought to make excuses for one another? It is easier to love those whom you see and to forgive their faults than to claim love for God whom you do not see. This is a higher degree for one who is able to love those he sees and then after that to love the One he does not see, who is God.

Be compassionate toward others and forgive quickly if they wrong you, remembering God's forgiveness of you throughout all your past life, knowing that whoever sins is a weak person who needs someone to pray for him and support him with love.
Christ guides us to eternal life

Whoever believes in the incarnate Christ and shows his faith in practice by loving others deserves to be called a child of God, since he has received the Sacrament of Baptism and lives by the new nature as a child of God, by his love for all. Whoever has become a child of God loves God his Father, and whoever loves God the Father, the Begetter, naturally loves the One begotten of Him, that is, Christ. He does not believe in Him only out of fear of Him, like the demons, but loves Him, so the proof of his sonship to God is his love for Christ.

If we love Christ, the Head of the Church, we therefore love His Body, that is, our brethren. What confirms that our love for the brethren is true spiritual love and not merely temporary human emotion is our love for God our Father, and if we love Him we keep His commandments and hold fast to them, and among the most important of these commandments is our love for others (Mt 22:39).

Our love for others is the sum of keeping God's commandments and the proof of our love for Him. Carrying out this love is not difficult, because Christ offered Himself as an example for us in loving others by laying down His life on the Cross, and by the grace of His Holy Spirit He enables us to love others, so that we have compassion even on those who wrong us and are hostile to us.
Our faith in Christ granted us sonship to Him by Baptism, and we received the new nature that overcomes the evil of the world by love for everyone, even for those who wrong us.

Do not be troubled by the wrongs of others, but ask for God's help and trust that He will support you and give you a compassionate heart toward them, so that you overcome their evil with your love, gain the salvation of your soul, and indeed draw them to Christ.

The witness of Christ, that is, His salvation offered to us, is through faith in His blood shed on the Cross, whose effect in us we receive in the Sacrament of Baptism. Christ did not come by water only, like the baptism of John the Baptist or any earlier baptisms, such as the baptizing of the proselytes of Judaism when they joined it, but He came with the water of Baptism and with His blood on the Cross. The Holy Spirit bears witness to Christ when He gives us the salvation accomplished on the Cross through the Sacraments of the Church, in Baptism and the other Sacraments, for He is the truth given to mankind in the Church.

The blood and water that came out of the side of Christ when they pierced Him on the Cross is a proof of His humanity, for He is the incarnate Son of God, and this refutes the heresies that reject the humanity of Christ which appeared in the first century, such as the heresy of the Docetists.

Those who bear witness in heaven to the salvation of Christ offered to mankind are the three hypostases, the Father, the Son (the Word) and the Holy Spirit, as they appeared at the baptism of Christ by John the Baptist, and these three hypostases are the attributes of one God. This verse is one of the clearest verses proving the Holy Trinity.

Three witnesses to the accomplishing of salvation appeared on the Cross: the human spirit united with the divinity, which Christ gave up at His death, and the blood and the water that came out of His side when they pierced Him. The three are one, that is, Christ who died for our redemption, and we receive the three who bear witness in the Sacrament of Baptism. When we are baptized the Holy Spirit takes the salvation accomplished by the blood of Christ on the Cross and sanctifies the water of Baptism, so that we are born from it with a new nature.

If we accept the witness of men, as the Law teaches us that "at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established" (Deut 19:15), then all the more should we accept the witness of God in His three hypostases at the baptism of Christ and at His death on the Cross, as we mentioned in the previous verse.
The witness in himself: the Holy Spirit working in man, who calls him to faith in Christ.

The Holy Spirit calls all people to faith in Christ, and when they believe and are baptized He dwells in them in the Sacrament of the Myron and establishes their faith. But whoever rejects the witness of God, that is, the Holy Spirit, and does not believe in Christ, describes God as a liar.
The Holy Spirit calls you to faith in God in every step of your daily life, so do not be troubled but believe God and rely on Him, and you will enjoy His blessings in your life.

The purpose of the witness of God in His three hypostases, and through the Church by the Holy Sacraments, is that we receive eternal life. We experience this eternal life partially by the work of Christ in us on earth, and it is completed in heaven by our union with Him and our enjoyment of His company. Eternal life is the salvation that we receive in Christ.
Whoever believes in Christ the Son and lives for Him receives eternal life, and whoever refuses faith and life with Christ has no place in the Kingdom of Heaven.
The purpose of this epistle is faith in Christ and abiding in Him so that we receive the eternal life prepared for us.

Our faith in Christ supports us so that we ask God for everything we want, trusting that He answers us, on condition that these requests are according to His will, that is, in agreement with our salvation and our attaining eternity.

A sin not unto death is any sin, however heinous, as long as the person is ready to repent of it, so we pray for him until he repents and receives forgiveness, salvation and eternal life. But whoever commits a sin unto death, that is, he persists in sin and refuses to repent of it, prayer will not benefit him. The Apostle did not command that we not pray for him but left it to the freedom of the one praying, according to his judgment whether there are motives driving him to persist which could be removed by prayer, or whether he is persisting in evil. In general, however, we do not know total persistence in evil until after the death of the sinner, such as suicides, for whom the Church refuses to pray, or those who denied the faith and died denying it. Therefore we continue to pray for all sinners as long as they are alive, that perhaps they will repent.
Unrighteousness: an infringement on the rights of others, as in the Greek original.
Sin: disobedience and violation of God's word.
Every wrong done to others is a weakness of love and can be turned back from through repentance, and so we are saved from eternal death.
Whoever has received the new nature in Baptism and lives as a child of God by his love for Him and for others, this love keeps him from the evils of sins, and Satan cannot make him fall into them.

We who believe in Christ, live in the Church and love everyone, enjoy our sonship to God and our communion with Him, and our conduct is different from that of the children of the world, who are subject to the devil and walk in evil.

The aim of the Incarnation of Christ is to enlighten our inner eyes by changing our nature in the Sacrament of Baptism, so that we know the truth, that is, we believe in Him and love Him and love others, and so have a share in eternal life with Him.

The Apostle reminds us of our sonship to God so that we keep our life in faith in Him and love for Him, and so keep away from idolatry, which is the various attachments of the world such as money, position and the various desires, and by this we keep away from Satan in all his forms and deceptions.

Do not forget your goal in the midst of the crowd of life's concerns, for your only goal is eternity, and your way to it is the love of Christ, by your attachment to the Church and your love for everyone.
